content: For complete information about this product and your specific health needs, consult your healthcare professional. Uses: Oseltamivir is prescribed to treat symptoms caused by the influenza virus (commonly known as the flu). It can also be used to prevent the flu if you have been exposed to someone infected (e.g., a sick household member) or during a community flu outbreak. This medication works by inhibiting the growth of the flu virus. However, it is not a replacement for the flu vaccine. How to Use: Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take oseltamivir orally, with or without food. To reduce stomach upset, you may take it with food or milk. For flu prevention, follow your doctor’s instructions, typically taking it once daily for at least 10 days. The dosage depends on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you cannot swallow capsules, ask your doctor or pharmacist about the liquid suspension form of oseltamivir. If the liquid form is unavailable, and if directed by your doctor or pharmacist, you may open the capsule and mix its contents with a small amount of sweetened liquid (e.g., regular or sugar-free chocolate syrup, corn syrup, caramel topping, or light brown sugar dissolved in water). For optimal results, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) each day. Continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Side Effects: Nausea and vomiting may occur. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, the flu itself or oseltamivir may cause serious mental or mood changes, which are more likely in children. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking oseltamivir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Oseltamivir passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Inform your doctor if you have received a nasal flu vaccine within two weeks before starting this medication, as oseltamivir may reduce the effectiveness of the nasal flu vaccine. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose (within 2 hours), skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. For further assistance, contact your healthcare provider or pharmacist.
